<cite ref="Ketubot 72b:4">Keth. 72ᵇ</cite> <he>קא שדיא פִילְכָהּ וטווה וכ׳</he> casting the spindle and spinning &c. (v. <cite ref="F00084"><he>וָרָד</he></cite>); <he>פסיקתיה לפילכה וכ׳</he> she broke (the thread of) her spindle and threw it away (as if it had accidentally slipped); <he>אמרה עולם הב לי פִילְכָאִי</he> Ar. (ed. <he>פלך</he>) she said, young man, hand me my spindle; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 95a:10">Snh. 95ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 155:4">Yalk. Sam. 155</cite>; a. e.—
Meg. 14ᵇ (prov.) אתתא בהדי שותא פילכא (sub. שדיא) a woman handles the shuttle while she talks, i.e. pursues two aims at a time; [Ar. s. v. שותא: פַּלְכָה spins.]
